intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple and the Bayon with its 216 serene stone faces.

experiences.name: Khmer Street Food Tour in Phnom Penh
experiences.description: Join a guided evening walk through the bustling streets of Phnom Penh sampling authentic Khmer dishes including fish amok, nom banh chok noodles, lok lak beef, and fresh sugar cane juice at local markets and street stalls, learning about Cambodia's culinary history.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine white-sand beaches of Koh Rong Samloem island, swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters, snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, and relax on the near-deserted Saracen Bay beach, one of Southeast Asia's most unspoiled coastal gems.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem Island, Sihanoukville

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields Tour
experiences.description: Visit the sobering S-21 prison turned museum and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial to gain a profound understanding of Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history. Audio guides and survivor testimonies provide deeply moving cultural and historical context.

experiences.name: Traditional Apsara Dance Performance and Cooking Class
experiences.description: Attend an elegant evening Apsara dance performance showcasing Cambodia's UNESCO-listed classical dance heritage, then spend the following morning in a hands-on Khmer cooking class learning to prepare traditional dishes using local spices and fresh market ingredients.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport, clear immigration and customs, arrange budget transport (shared taxi or bus) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and cheap bite at a local 24-hour street food stall near the resort if hungry upon arrival (budget $2–4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some small USD bills handy for tips and transport. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Arrange airport pickup in advance or use a metered tuk-tuk to save money. Do not exchange currency at the airport — rates are poor.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, explore the immediate beachfront area on foot. Walk along the beach, get your bearings, and enjoy the coastal scenery. Visit a local morning market nearby to sample fresh tropical fruits and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) and explore the surrounding coastal village. Visit a local Buddhist temple (wat) in the area for a first taste of Cambodian culture and architecture. Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Head to a local seafood shack on the beach for a fresh and affordable dinner. Enjoy the relaxed coastal atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local market breakfast — rice porridge (borbor) or fresh fruit and iced coffee ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Street food noodle soup (kuy teav) from a roadside stall near the resort ($1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish or squid at a beachfront seafood shack with rice ($4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather with low humidity. Perfect beach conditions. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. Budget for the day: approximately $15–20 USD including meals, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget boat trip to a nearby island (if located near Sihanoukville or Kep coastal area). Explore the island on foot, snorkel in the clear waters, and relax on quieter beaches. Many budget boat tours depart early morning ($5–10 USD round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the island. Visit a local fishing village near the resort to observe traditional Cambodian coastal life. Interact with locals, watch fishermen bring in their catch, and browse small local shops for inexpensive souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost traditional Khmer cultural performance if available locally. Otherwise, stroll the night market for street food and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Baguette with pâté or egg (French-Khmer fusion, a Cambodian staple) from a street vendor ($1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch of bread, fruit, and water from a local market for the island trip ($3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — try lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice) or amok (fish curry) ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Negotiate boat prices in advance. Avoid single-use plastics on the island to help preserve the environment. Total budget for the day: approximately $20–25 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by budget bus or shared minivan toward Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Book tickets in advance through guesthouses or online platforms like Bookmebus ($6–10 USD). Journey takes approximately 4–5 hours depending on your coastal starting point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check into a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area ($8–15/night). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of Khmer royal architecture. Entry fee approximately $6.25 USD. Dress modestly.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Tonle Sap and Mekong Riverside promenade. Explore the bustling night market (Phsar Reatrey) for street food, local snacks, and cheap souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort or bus station before departure — rice and fried egg ($2 USD)
meals.lunch: Stop at a local restaurant en route or near the bus station in Phnom Penh — Khmer noodles or rice with curry ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Riverside street food stalls — try nom banh chok (Khmer noodles) or grilled corn and skewers ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Store your luggage at the Phnom Penh guesthouse before exploring. Tuk-tuks in Phnom Penh are affordable ($1–3 per short ride). Use PassApp or Grab app for metered tuk-tuks to avoid overcharging. Total budget for the day: approximately $30–40 USD including transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply important and sobering historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities. Entry fee $3 USD. Audio guides available for $3 USD extra. Spend 2–3 hours here to absorb the history respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (approximately 15 km from city center). Take a tuk-tuk ($5–7 round trip). Entry fee $6 USD including an audio guide. This UNESCO-recognized memorial is essential for understanding modern Cambodian history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Phnom Penh. Visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives the city its name. Free to enter or small donation. Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for local goods and bargain shopping.

meals.breakfast: Local café near guesthouse — French bread with butter and jam, iced coffee ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Cheap Khmer lunch restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice with stir-fried vegetables and pork ($2.50–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget Khmer restaurant near the Riverside — try fish amok (national dish) with rice ($4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Genocide Museum and Killing Fields are emotionally heavy. Take time to process and be respectful. Photography is permitted in some areas but always be mindful of the solemnity. Total budget for the day: approximately $25–35 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the National Museum of Cambodia (Phsar Kandal area) — one of Southeast Asia's finest collections of Khmer art and artifacts. Entry fee $5 USD. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring ancient sculptures, ceramics, and bronzes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget bus or shared minivan from Phnom Penh to Kampot ($5–7 USD, approximately 3 hours). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town famous for its pepper, relaxed vibe, and nearby Bokor Hill Station.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kampot. Check into a budget guesthouse ($6–12/night). Take a relaxed sunset boat ride on the Kampot River (many guesthouses offer this for $5–8 USD). Explore the old French colonial town center on foot.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Phnom Penh — eggs, toast, and coffee ($3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Grab food at the Phnom Penh bus station or eat on the bus — packed snacks and drinks ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Kampot riverside restaurant — fresh Kampot pepper crab or fish with rice ($5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is one of Cambodia's most beloved budget traveler destinations. Rent a bicycle or motorbike the next day to explore the area. November weather in Kampot is ideal — dry and breezy. Total budget for the day: approximately $25–35 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike ($5–8/day) or bicycle ($2–3/day) and ride up to Bokor Hill Station — a dramatic abandoned French colonial hill resort at 1,080 meters elevation. Explore the eerie old casino, church ruins, and palace with stunning views over the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Bokor and visit a local Kampot pepper farm for a free or low-cost tour. Learn about Cambodia's world-famous pepper cultivation. Purchase affordable fresh pepper directly from farmers as a unique souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot town. Relax at a riverside bar or café. Enjoy a cheap happy hour drink (draft beer $0.50–1 USD at many local bars) and watch the fireflies emerge over the river at dusk — a magical Kampot experience.

meals.breakfast: Local market breakfast in Kampot — rice porridge with fish ($1.50–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Simple roadside restaurant near Bokor — fried rice or noodles ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget Khmer restaurant in Kampot town — lok lak or green mango salad with rice ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The road up Bokor is paved but steep — ensure your motorbike is in good condition. Bring a light jacket as Bokor can be cool and misty at the top. Total budget for the day: approximately $20–28 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short shared taxi or tuk-tuk from Kampot to Kep ($3–5 USD, 30 minutes). Kep is a tiny, tranquil former French resort town famous for its crab market and beautiful coastline. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a unique floating market where you can buy fresh crabs directly from fishermen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kep National Park — hike the jungle trail (approximately 8 km loop, free entry) through dense forest with wildlife including monkeys and exotic birds. Visit the abandoned villas of former Khmer Rouge-era ruins hidden in the jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot (or stay in Kep at a budget guesthouse $8–15/night). Enjoy a farewell dinner featuring Kep's signature dish — Kep crab with Kampot pepper sauce — a must-try Cambodian delicacy.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Kampot before departure ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh crab cooked at the Kep Crab Market — buy raw crab and have it cooked on-site ($4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant in Kep — Kampot pepper crab with bread and salad ($6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Kep is very small and easily explored in a day. Combine with Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) if time allows — a 20-minute boat ride ($5 return) to a pristine beach with hammock bungalows. Total budget for the day: approximately $25–35 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the beach resort area (Aegean Bliss Resort) by shared taxi or bus from Kampot/Kep ($5–8 USD). Spend the morning relaxing on the beach, swimming, or kayaking (kayak rentals typically $3–5/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Cambodian village inland from the resort. Hire a tuk-tuk driver to take you on a half-day cultural tour of surrounding villages ($8–12 USD for the tuk-tuk). Visit a local school, pagoda, and rice fields to experience authentic rural Cambodian life.
day_by_day.evening: Final beach sunset — find the best spot on the beach to watch the sun sink into the Gulf of Thailand. Treat yourself to a slightly splurge-worthy final dinner at a beachfront restaurant to celebrate your last full evening.

meals.breakfast: Roadside breakfast stop en route back to the resort — Khmer noodle soup ($1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and light snacks on the beach ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood dinner — grilled prawns, squid, and rice with a cold Angkor beer ($8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Good budget souvenirs include Kampot pepper, Khmer scarves (krama), handmade crafts, and local spices. Total budget for the day: approximately $30–40 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. Arrange transport to the airport well in advance (shared taxi or airport shuttle $10–20 USD depending on distance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, use any remaining hours to visit a nearby local market for last-minute shopping, or relax at a café with iced Cambodian coffee (cafe toek kak) and reflect on your journey.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your departure. Enjoy a final Cambodian meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before flying home.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby café — fresh fruit platter, eggs, and iced coffee ($3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the airport or en route — fried rice with chicken or vegetables ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or pre-departure meal — Khmer noodles or a light snack ($4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep USD cash for airport departure tax if not included in your ticket. Confirm your flight details the night before. Exchange any remaining Cambodian Riel back to USD before leaving (USD is widely used so you may have little riel). Total budget for the day: approximately $20–30 USD. Estimated total 10-day trip budget: $220–320 USD excluding flights and accommodation, covering meals, local transport, activities, and entrance fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). Check in, freshen up, and unwind. Take a short stroll along the beachfront promenade if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: On flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: On flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — try a light Cambodian noodle soup (Kuy Teav) if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm resort transfer in advance. Exchange some USD or local Riel at the airport for small expenses. Cambodia widely accepts USD.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast at the resort, take a relaxing walk along the beachfront to orient yourself. Explore the immediate resort surroundings and nearby beach stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local village or town nearest to the resort for a gentle cultural introduction. Browse small markets, interact with locals, and pick up fresh tropical fruit from roadside stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beach bar or a nearby beachfront restaurant. Enjoy the calm Gulf of Thailand atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fresh fruit, rice porridge (Bobor), eggs
meals.lunch: Local eatery near the resort — Fish Amok (steamed fish curry in banana leaf) ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant near resort — grilled prawns, stir-fried morning glory, steamed rice ~$12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. No heavy sightseeing planned. Sunscreen and insect repellent are essential. November weather in coastal Cambodia is generally warm and mostly dry.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip to a nearby island (e.g., Koh Rong or Koh Rong Samloem if near Sihanoukville). Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear waters and explore the coral reef ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on a secluded white-sand beach on the island. Swim, read, or join a guided kayaking session around the island's coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon boat. Freshen up and head to a local night market for street food exploration.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — baguette with jam (French-Khmer influence), tropical fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Island beach shack — fresh grilled fish, coconut rice, cold Angkor beer ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Night market street food — BBQ skewers, Lok Lak (stir-fried beef), fresh spring rolls ~$6–10

day_by_day.notes: Book island boat trips through the resort or a local tour operator the evening before. Bring waterproof bags, reef-safe sunscreen, and cash for island vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby historical or cultural site. Visit a local Khmer temple or pagoda in the region — even coastal areas have beautiful wats (Buddhist temples) worth exploring with a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a traditional Cambodian fishing village by tuk-tuk or bicycle. Observe daily life, watch fishermen mend nets, and learn about the local fishing economy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a traditional Khmer cooking class offered by the resort or a local culinary school — learn to make Fish Amok and mango salad.

meals.breakfast: Resort café — Khmer-style rice with fried egg and pickled vegetables
meals.lunch: Local family restaurant in fishing village — set Khmer lunch with soup, rice, and curry ~$5–7
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner — eat what you cook! Pair with fresh coconut water or local Cambodian beer

day_by_day.notes: Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–25) for flexibility. Dress modestly when visiting temples — cover shoulders and knees. Cooking classes should be booked 1 day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a domestic flight or private transfer from the coastal region to Siem Reap (approximately 1–2 hours by air or 7–8 hours by road — flight recommended for mid-range budget). Check in to a mid-range guesthouse in Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for an excellent introduction to the Khmer Empire, Angkor Wat's history, and Buddhist art before visiting the temples.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Siem Reap's vibrant Pub Street and Old Market (Phsar Chas) area. Browse handicrafts, silk scarves, and Apsara dancer figurines.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Airport or roadside stop — Banh Mi sandwich or rice dish ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Pub Street restaurant — Khmer red curry, fried rice with vegetables, fresh lime juice ~$10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights (Cambodian Bayon Airlines or similar) well in advance. Angkor National Museum entry is ~$12 USD. Siem Reap mid-range hotels average $30–60/night. Tuk-tuks are the best way to get around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:30 AM) to witness the iconic sunrise over Angkor Wat — one of the world's most spectacular sights. Explore the outer galleries, bas-relief carvings depicting Hindu mythology, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider temple') as the afternoon crowds thin out — marvel at massive tree roots engulfing ancient stone structures. Return to Siem Reap for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early packed snack or coffee before sunrise — pick up from a local stall near Angkor Wat entrance
meals.lunch: Restaurant near Angkor Thom — set Khmer lunch with Amok, soup, and rice ~$7–10
meals.dinner: Traditional Khmer restaurant in Siem Reap with live Apsara dance performance — ~$15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass (~$62 USD) — valid for Days 6, 7, and 8. Start sunrise visit by 5:00 AM. Hire a knowledgeable local tuk-tuk driver/guide for the day (~$20–30). Carry plenty of water — it gets hot even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer Angkor circuit: Visit Preah Khan (a vast jungle temple), Neak Pean (an island temple on an artificial lake), and Ta Som (a small but beautifully atmospheric temple).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Eastern Mebon and Pre Rup temples — Pre Rup's elevated platform offers panoramic views over the jungle canopy, ideal for late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor Wat complex again at sunset for a completely different atmospheric experience. Then explore the Siem Reap Night Market for local crafts and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — French-press coffee, banana pancakes, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Jungle temple area food stall — fried rice, spring rolls, cold coconut ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Siem Reap mid-range restaurant — Beef Lok Lak, green mango salad, Angkor draft beer ~$12–16

day_by_day.notes: Use your 3-day Angkor pass. Preah Khan and Neak Pean are less crowded than Angkor Wat — great for photography. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and refillable water bottle. Bargain respectfully at the Night Market.

day_by_day.morning: Final Angkor day — explore the lesser-visited but stunning Banteay Srei temple, known as the 'Citadel of Women' and famous for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. Located ~25 km north of Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Samré temple en route back, then stop at the Landmine Museum (Aki Ra's Museum) — a powerful and important cultural site about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a riverside café along the Siem Reap River. Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local cultural center if not already experienced.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Congee (rice porridge) with ginger and spring onion
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Banteay Srei — Khmer noodle soup, papaya salad ~$6–9
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Khmer fusion restaurant in Siem Reap — Khmer tasting menu ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is covered by the Angkor pass. The Landmine Museum charges a small donation (~$3–5). Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day (~$25–35) as Banteay Srei is farther from the main complex. This is your last Angkor day — savor it.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Phnom Penh by bus or private transfer (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by domestic flight). Check in to a mid-range hotel in the capital.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring gilded spires and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. Admire the Emerald Buddha.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade. Watch the sunset over the Tonle Sap and Mekong River confluence. Explore the lively riverfront bar and restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure
meals.lunch: En route — roadside Cambodian restaurant or bus stop — rice with grilled pork ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Riverfront restaurant in Phnom Penh — fresh Mekong fish, stir-fried vegetables, rice ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: Bus tickets from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh cost ~$10–15 (Giant Ibis or Mekong Express are reputable). Royal Palace entry ~$10 USD. Dress code strictly enforced — no shorts or sleeveless tops. Mid-range Phnom Penh hotels average $35–65/night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply sobering but essential historical site that documents the Khmer Rouge atrocities. Hire an audio guide or local guide for full context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — Southeast Asia's largest archaeological museum housing thousands of Khmer artifacts, sculptures, and bronzes spanning 2,000 years of history. Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking Phnom Penh's skyline. Reflect on the journey — from beaches to ancient temples to the capital's complex history.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — French baguette, pâté, coffee (Phnom Penh's French colonial legacy)
meals.lunch: Central Market food court — Khmer noodles, fresh fruit shake, iced coffee ~$4–7
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant, Phnom Penh — Khmer set dinner with Amok, Lok Lak, and dessert ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng entry ~$8 USD. The museum is emotionally intense — allow time to process. National Museum entry ~$10 USD. Pack souvenirs carefully — silk scarves, Khmer pepper, and handmade crafts make excellent gifts. Confirm departure logistics and airport transfer for your return flight.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer with a dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a welcome sign. Enjoy a chilled towel and refreshments in the vehicle en route to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your beachfront suite, enjoy a complimentary welcome amenity (champagne and fruit platter) arranged by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining available upon arrival — recommend the resort's 24-hour room service featuring Khmer-inspired late-night bites such as amok curry with jasmine rice and fresh tropical fruit

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Pack light carry-on essentials for easy late-night check-in. Request early turndown service and next-day breakfast preferences to be set tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. After breakfast, take a private guided orientation tour of the resort grounds and beachfront. Spend time acclimatizing with a relaxing swim in the infinity pool or a gentle stroll along the private beach. Optional: book a 60-minute welcome spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa to recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate coastal village near the resort with a private tuk-tuk tour. Visit local fishing communities and observe traditional boat-building crafts. Stop at a nearby coastal market to browse fresh seafood, handmade crafts, and Cambodian spices. Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail session on the beach terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront dinner under the stars arranged by the resort — a curated multi-course Khmer tasting menu featuring freshly caught seafood, lemongrass-infused broths, and coconut-based desserts, served with torchlit ambiance and live traditional Cambodian music.

meals.breakfast: Resort's beachfront restaurant — à la carte luxury breakfast featuring fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), eggs Benedict, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort cabana — grilled prawns, mango salad, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront tasting dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — 5-course Khmer seafood menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day after the late arrival. Confirm spa appointment in advance. The private tuk-tuk tour can be arranged through the resort concierge at no extra hassle.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private speedboat or chartered vessel for a premium island-hopping excursion off the Cambodian coastline (Koh Rong or Koh Rong Sanloem islands if near Sihanoukville, or equivalent coastal islands near your resort location). Snorkel in crystal-clear waters over vibrant coral reefs with a private guide and all premium snorkeling gear provided. Enjoy a secluded beach landing on an uninhabited island for a private picnic setup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island exploration — visit a hidden lagoon accessible only by kayak or small boat. Enjoy paddleboarding, kayaking, or simply relaxing on pristine white-sand beaches. A private butler accompanies the excursion with chilled beverages, sunscreen, and towels. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's sky bar or rooftop terrace. Dress for a refined dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring contemporary Cambodian cuisine with French culinary influences — think duck amok with truffle oil, Kampot pepper-crusted lobster, and palm sugar crème brûlée.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh pastries, yogurt, tropical fruits, and espresso
meals.lunch: Private picnic on the island — gourmet hamper with artisan sandwiches, fresh ceviche, tropical fruit, sparkling water, and Champagne
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — contemporary Khmer-French fusion tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the private speedboat charter at least 24 hours in advance through the concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light cover-up. Check weather conditions for boat safety.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered flight or premium vehicle transfer to Siem Reap (approximately 1–1.5 hours by air). Upon arrival, check in to a pre-arranged luxury day suite or partner hotel. Begin the iconic Angkor temple experience with an exclusive private guided tour of Angkor Wat at sunrise — arrive before crowds for an ethereal golden-hour experience at one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs, towers, and reflecting pools with your expert Khmer historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the magnificent Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Terrace of the Elephants, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private air-conditioned vehicle for all transfers between temples. Stop for a curated lunch break at a premium restaurant near the temples.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town for a luxury dinner at one of the city's acclaimed restaurants. Attend an exclusive private Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized traditional Khmer dance art form — arranged in an intimate heritage setting.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before transfer or at the Siem Reap partner hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Restaurant, Siem Reap — acclaimed fine-dining Cambodian cuisine in a heritage garden setting
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant or The Sugar Palm, Siem Reap — authentic royal Khmer cuisine with private Apsara dance performance

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Archaeological Park requires a pass — your concierge will pre-purchase a 3-day pass for the Angkor temple days. Wear light, breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes for temple exploration. Respect temple dress codes (covered shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive early morning hot air balloon ride over the Angkor temple complex at sunrise for a breathtaking aerial perspective of the ancient city (tethered balloon available near Angkor Wat). Afterward, visit the mystical Ta Prohm temple — famously engulfed by giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees — with your private guide. Explore Preah Khan temple, a sprawling jungle monastery with stunning stone corridors and carved devata figures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the lesser-known but equally stunning Banteay Srei temple — the 'Citadel of Women' — renowned for its exquisitely detailed pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest example of Khmer art. En route, stop at a traditional silk weaving village to observe artisans at work and shop for premium Cambodian silk scarves and textiles as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the FCC Angkor rooftop or Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor terrace bar overlooking the Siem Reap cityscape. Dinner at a celebrated chef's table experience — a private multi-course dinner prepared by a renowned local chef highlighting Cambodia's royal culinary heritage.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack before balloon ride; full breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel after return
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the hotel, enjoyed in the shade of the Angkor temple grounds
meals.dinner: Private chef's table dinner at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or equivalent luxury property — royal Khmer tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon rides are weather-dependent and should be booked well in advance. Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km from Siem Reap — factor in travel time. The silk village visit supports local artisan communities.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise visit to the remote and atmospheric Beng Mealea temple — a 12th-century Angkorian masterpiece largely unrestored and dramatically overgrown by jungle vegetation. Explore its collapsed galleries, moss-covered stones, and hidden chambers with a private expert guide. The site is far less visited, offering an Indiana Jones-style adventure in complete luxury comfort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Roluos Group of temples — among the oldest in the Angkor region, including Preah Ko, Bakong, and Lolei — for a deeper understanding of the evolution of Khmer architecture. Stop at the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a curated private tour of its extraordinary collection of Khmer artifacts, sculptures, and historical chronicles.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Siem Reap evening — enjoy a luxury river cruise on the Tonlé Sap Lake at sunset aboard a private wooden boat, with cocktails and canapés served on deck as the sky turns golden. Transfer back to the resort via premium private vehicle or chartered flight the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure to Beng Mealea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium countryside restaurant near Beng Mealea or a packed gourmet picnic basket
meals.dinner: Private sunset dinner cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — freshwater fish specialties, Khmer tapas, and Cambodian craft cocktails served on board

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea is approximately 68 km from Siem Reap — allow 90 minutes travel each way. Wear sturdy footwear as the terrain is uneven. The Tonlé Sap cruise should be booked through a premium local operator.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer back to the Aegean Bliss Resort (via chartered flight or luxury vehicle). Upon return, enjoy a late morning recovery session — indulge in a signature 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa, featuring traditional Khmer massage techniques using locally sourced herbs, lemongrass, and kaffir lime oils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure on the resort's private beach. Enjoy water sports activities available at the resort — options may include stand-up paddleboarding, jet skiing, parasailing, or a guided snorkeling session in the resort's reef area. Alternatively, relax in a private beach cabana with butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Cambodian cooking class hosted by the resort's executive chef — learn to prepare three signature Khmer dishes including fish amok, green mango salad, and sticky rice with palm sugar. Enjoy your creations as dinner in a beautiful garden or beachfront setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel before transfer
meals.lunch: Poolside or beachside light lunch at the resort upon return — fresh coconut, grilled fish, and tropical salads
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private Khmer cooking class, enjoyed in the resort's garden dining space with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the spa appointment and cooking class with the resort concierge before the Siem Reap trip. The cooking class is a premium add-on experience and a wonderful cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Phnom Penh, Cambodia's vibrant capital (by chartered flight or premium vehicle). Begin with a sobering but essential visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — an architectural masterpiece of Khmer design featuring sacred Buddha statues, the Emerald Buddha, and stunning murals of the Reamker epic. Explore with a private historian guide for deep cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts spanning 2,000 years of history. Explore the museum's serene courtyard and galleries at a leisurely pace. Afterward, stroll through the charming French Quarter of Phnom Penh — admire colonial architecture, boutique galleries, and artisan shops along the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong and Tonlé Sap river confluence. Dinner at Phnom Penh's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurant before returning to the resort via private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Topaz Restaurant or Malis Phnom Penh — sophisticated Cambodian cuisine in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven One Kitchen or Khéma Pasteur, Phnom Penh — contemporary Cambodian and French cuisine with exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Memorial are also available for those wishing to understand Cambodia's modern history — these are deeply moving sites and recommended for historically minded travelers. Dress respectfully for the Royal Palace visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — wake up early for a private sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor. Follow with a refreshing ocean swim and a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the beachfront restaurant. Spend the morning on a private chartered fishing boat excursion with a local expert fisherman — try your hand at traditional Cambodian fishing techniques and enjoy the serene coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final indulgent spa afternoon — book the resort's signature half-day wellness journey including a body scrub with Cambodian rice and coconut, a deep-tissue Khmer massage, and a facial using local botanical ingredients. Conclude with a relaxing soak in a flower-petal bath in your suite.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's most prestigious dining venue — a private table on the beach set with candles, flowers, and personalized décor arranged by the concierge. A curated 7-course degustation menu celebrating the finest flavors of Cambodia — from Kampot pepper crab to coconut sticky rice — paired with premium wines and finishing with a Champagne toast.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet beachfront breakfast at the resort — full spread including fresh seafood, tropical fruits, pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the fishing boat or back at the resort's beach club — grilled catch of the day with fresh herbs and lime
meals.dinner: Private 7-course farewell degustation dinner on the beach at Aegean Bliss Resort — sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request the personalized farewell dinner setup at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. The fishing excursion is a wonderful cultural experience and can be combined with a seafood cooking demonstration back at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy one last swim in the ocean or pool, a slow breakfast, and time to pack. Visit the resort's boutique to pick up premium Cambodian souvenirs — artisan silk products, Kampot pepper sets, handcrafted jewelry, and local coffee blends. Arrange a final spa treatment or reflexology session if time permits before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort with a full concierge-assisted departure. Private luxury transfer to the airport with ample time before your departure flight. The resort will arrange a farewell gift bag with Cambodian artisan products and a personalized note from the team.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — carry with you memories of ancient temples, pristine beaches, rich Khmer culture, and world-class hospitality. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely breakfast at the resort — order your favorites from the à la carte menu as a send-off treat
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge depending on flight timing — the resort can prepare a gourmet takeaway box for the journey
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your next destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and airport transfer with the concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Request a late checkout if your flight departs in the evening — most luxury resorts accommodate this with advance notice.
